newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bangkok Bank snags 144a bond.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bangkok Bank snags 144a bond.

text.p: Bangkok Bank became the second Thai issuer to access the U.S. market in 1997 with a US$300 million 144a bond launched overnight in New York.
Asian debt markets were otherwise quiet on Thursday.
Bangkok Bank launched the 8.375 percent bond due 2027 at par to yield 155 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
The borrower, which is the premier bank in Thailand, is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB-plus by Standard and Poor's Corp.
The initial size of the issue was US$150 million but the amount was increased to meet investor demand, U.S. dealers said.
Interest in Thai debt issues declined in the latter half of 1996 as political and economic uncertainty depressed the country's financial markets generally.

Chris Tuffey, head of syndicate for the Asia-Pacific region for CS First Boston, said that while there were few signs that investors were unloading Thai securities last year "what we have seen over the last few months is a buyer strike where (investors) refuse to add to their positions."

"But I think with the increased supply we are seeing now with IFCT and Bangkok Bank and the PTTEP transaction we had last year, we are seeing people back into the market to look at Thai names again," Tuffey told Reuters Financial Television in its weekly Asian Debt Briefing.

Alan Yamashita, managing director of debt and capital markets at Merrill Lynch, said that while investor sentiment has been cautious, he was very encouraged by the market response to the Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand (IFCT) Euro 144a bond Merrill launched last week.
The US$200 million 10-year bond was priced last Friday to yield 90 basis points over comparable Treasuries. It was trading at 86-89 basis points today.
"We think that investors had been underweight Thailand and that they will cautiously come back to the market," said Yamashita.
In other debt news, State Development Bank of China on Wednesday filed a shelf registration with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to sell up to US$300 million in notes.
Lehman Brothers and J.P. Morgan Securities are lead managers for the State Development Bank deal.
Standard and Poor's Corp assigned BB long-term and Single-B short term counterparty ratings to Indonesia's Bank Niaga.

Asian investment bank Peregrine Investments Holdings said it plans to seek ratings from S&P and Moody's Investors Service after receiving a BBB-plus rating from the Japan Bond Research Institute on its unsecured long-term debt.
